stem: A dataset has arithmetic mean 40 and standard deviation 10. What is its coefficient of variation?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Inverted the ratio: (Mean / SD) x 100 = (40 / 10) x 100 = 400%, then misread; or computed Mean itself as the percentage, giving 40%. This conflates mean with CV.
Computed (SD / Mean) = 10 / 40 = 0.25 but omitted the x 100 multiplication, yielding 0.25 then reading it as 4% after a further misplacement.
Used inverted formula (Mean / SD) x 100 = (40 / 10) x 100 = 400%.

explanation: CV = (Standard Deviation / Mean) x 100 = (10 / 40) x 100 = 25%. The CV expresses variability as a percentage of the mean, making datasets with different units or magnitudes comparable.

explanation_sections.punchline: CV is always SD divided by Mean, multiplied by 100 - not the other way around.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the formula: CV = (SD / Mean) x 100. Map givens: SD = 10, Mean = 40. Substitute and compute: 10/40 = 0.25; multiply by 100 to get 25%.
explanation_sections.lesson: CV = (SD / Mean) x 100. Inversion gives a number greater than 100 when mean exceeds SD, which is a quick sanity check.
explanation_sections.timing: About 25 seconds. Direct plug-in. The trap is inverting the fraction (Mean/SD), giving 400%.
